拾.meaning: A tidy sailor never drops his <part>anchor</part> for nothing. Each time he hauls it up, something is hooked on it: a boot, a bottle, a teapot lid that's a perfect <part>fit</part> for his own teapot. The bay is spotless now. He sails around just to <kanji>pick up</kanji> litter.
拾.on: Today the anchor brings up one giant <sound>shoe</sound>, full of crabs.
拾.kun: The shoe has a broken <sound>hee</sound>l and a toy <sound>ro</sound>cket stuck in its toe.

胎.meaning: A tiny astronaut floats in a warm round capsule with no windows, tethered by a cord. Each night his mum rests her bump on a pillow like a <part>pedestal</part> and sings to him under the <part>moon</part>. In nine months he'll land. For now, his spaceship is the <kanji>womb</kanji>.
胎.on: His dad is already practising his smartest <sound>tie</sound> knot for the big day.

宙.meaning: Under the <part>roof</part> of his workshop, a professor pins up a note with the <part>reason</part> things fall: gravity. A balloon knocks out the pin and the note drifts away. Now the teapot, the cat and the professor all bob below the ceiling. Without the reason, everything hangs in <kanji>mid-air</kanji>.
宙.on: The professor blows a bubble of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum and steers himself to the door with it.

維.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> perches on a sleeping farmer's ankle, tugs a loose <part>thread</part> from his sock and flies off with it. The sock gets shorter and shorter; by noon he's barefoot and her nest is woolly. Under a magnifying glass, each strand is a thousand hairs: <kanji>fiber</kanji> after fiber.
維.on: An <sound>ee</sound>l in the pond asks to borrow some to knit a scarf.

繊.meaning: A tightrope walker stretches one <part>thread</part> from a <part>spear</part> stuck in the <part>soil</part> to a stand of <part>candles</part> on the town hall roof. She tiptoes across so lightly the flames don't flicker. The crowd gasps: she and her thread are both so <kanji>slender</kanji>.
繊.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try below holds out a net, just in case.

宇.meaning: A wizard's cottage has a <part>roof</part> so wide its edges stick out far past the walls. Visitors hang their pointy hats on the <part>hat stand</part> by his door and stay dry while it pours, and pigeons nest all along the overhang. The best seat in the rain is under the <kanji>eaves</kanji>.
宇.on: There the wizard slurps a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don while the rain drums above.

喪.meaning: Since the old dog died, the boy wears his grandad's black <part>garment</part> every day. <part>Ten</part> times a day his <part>mouth</part> opens to whistle for her, and then he remembers. The house is quiet, and nobody tells him to stop. It's normal to <kanji>miss</kanji> someone.
喪.on: He keeps her collar beside the <sound>soa</sound>p in the bathroom, where he sees it every morning.
喪.kun: At dusk a grey <sound>mo</sound>th settles on his black sleeve and stays very still.
